faq.question: What time do Guangzhou night markets open and close?
faq.answer: Most Guangzhou night markets start around 5-6 PM and run until midnight or later. Zhicun Night Market is busiest from 7-11 PM. Baoye Road stays open until 2-3 AM for ye xiao (midnight supper). Shangxiajiu shops close around 10 PM but food stalls stay open later. Arrive after 7 PM for the best atmosphere.

faq.question: How do I pay at Guangzhou night markets?
faq.answer: WeChat Pay and Alipay dominate — nearly every stall accepts mobile payment via QR code. Alipay offers a "Tour Pass" mode for foreign tourists. Cash (RMB) is still accepted but some vendors may not carry change. Bring small denominations (¥10, ¥20) as backup. International credit cards are generally NOT accepted at street stalls.

faq.question: Is street food safe to eat at Guangzhou night markets?
faq.answer: Guangzhou has stricter food safety regulations than many Chinese cities — street food was technically banned and vendors must have proper ventilation and permits. Stick to busy stalls with high turnover. Watch for vendors wearing gloves and masks. Avoid raw foods and anything sitting at room temperature. Reddit consensus: "the busier the stall, the safer the food."

faq.question: What are the must-try foods at Guangzhou night markets?
faq.answer: Essential foods include: BBQ skewers (shaokao) with cumin, Cheung Fun (rice noodle rolls) with sweet soy sauce, Boat Congee (ting zai zhou) with shrimp and fish, Double-Skin Milk (shuangpi nai) — silky smooth dessert, Claypot Rice (bao zai fan) with Chinese sausage, Wonton Noodles in rich chicken broth, and Ham Sui Gok — crispy fried dumplings.

faq.question: Which Guangzhou night market is best for first-time visitors?
faq.answer: Shangxiajiu Pedestrian Street is the most accessible — well-lit, central, with a mix of traditional snacks and sit-down restaurants. For the most "local" experience, head to Zhicun Night Market near Yuancun Metro — where Guangzhou residents actually eat, with rock-bottom prices (¥15-50 per person).

faq.question: How do I get to Guangzhou night markets by metro?
faq.answer: Guangzhou's metro makes night markets easy to reach: Zhicun/Yuancun — Line 5, Yuancun Station Exit C; Shangxiajiu — Line 1, Changshou Lu Station; Beijing Road — Line 1 or 2, Gongyuanqian Station; Huangsha Seafood Market — Line 1 or 6, Huangsha Station. Metro runs until 11-11:30 PM. For late-night markets like Baoye Road, take DiDi.

faq.question: How much money should I budget for a night market evening?
faq.answer: Guangzhou night markets are incredibly affordable. Budget ¥30-50 at local markets like Zhicun or Longdong. Shangxiajiu and Beijing Road are ¥50-100. Huangsha Seafood Market runs ¥100-200+ for a proper seafood feast. For a full evening with drinks, ¥100-150 ($14-20 USD) per person is generous.
